semantics.ui_estimated_memory_current_working_budg: Expected to use about first formatted RAM quantity. Second line gives RAM currently usable for image work and second formatted quantity. Both placeholders and two literal Android newlines preserved.
semantics.ui_no_resize_fits_decoder_memory: Even at smallest output, cannot open this image for drawing/editing using currently usable RAM. Replaces decoder-only mechanism with full loading outcome. Exact current cancel-and-smaller-source sentence retained.
semantics.ui_assembly_source_memory_floor: Assembly expected to use more than current image-work RAM even at smallest output. Reducing assembly size alone leaves RAM insufficient. Close other documents remaining open in applications OR prepare smaller source, then retry. Assembly unchanged.

rejectedAlternatives: End-using alone could permit pausing without closing.
Physical-close alone without open software-document context.
Relative estimated-RAM label across thought complement; simpler finite sentence chosen.
Historical software attestation or native certification as mandatory gate.

independentReview.estimate: Agreed, prefer finite estimate sentence %1$s pakno RAM a=eywanke kuni a=ramu. It avoids long-distance head extraction and makes proposition scope explicit.
independentReview.loading: I support the loading-warning first sentence semantically: tan noka a=nuye kusu a=maka is opening the input for editing, not a codec-only process, and tane a=eywanke easkay RAM ani makes the current usable RAM constraint explicit. Keep medium idiom confidence and note inherited second sentence not independently perfected.
independentReview.assembly: I support the exact four-sentence assembly warning candidate you sent, with medium idiom confidence and bounded modern open/close metaphor. Aeywankep or ta + a=makpa wa oka explicitly identifies documents kept open within software tools, so roski now gives an actionable closing operation, not mere hiding or pausing work. The plurality accords with other documents; hene ... hene ki wa suy ki keeps alternatives before retry. Current-usable RAM insufficiency remains scoped to reducing assembly size alone.
independentReview.kana: Confirmed by manual clause/token comparison: your exact Kana assembly-warning, estimate-label and loading-warning renderings match the supported Latin, including a=makpa → アマㇰパ (stem-final k, not geminate), roski → ロㇱキ, the a= prefixes, RAM identifiers, both placeholders and escaped newlines.

review.scope_statement: Three exact resource keys per script. Medium idiom confidence; not whole-catalogue acceptance. Loading warning retains its current second sentence, not independently perfected.
